items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: we'd go into the picture with Rudolph Valentino.

ctx.x: He says, are you not a trumpet?

I said, I know it backwards. I stood up and played the whole overture from beginning to end, and when I got to the finish, I took it as a tactical, and the house come down there, and I never heard a trumpet player play the poet and peasant over to you on the trumpet. So that's the way you put yourself over. I made the only decent broadcast, the first decent broadcast in the city of New Orleans. When I was at Liberty, I was playing the Full Horseman from the Apocalypse. And I had Madame Guipaul, who was a leading…

You didn't get that. I didn't know it was duck soup though. I thought it was Ron Sophie. Did you hear what I said in the last one, won't you go? Yeah, I know. You go. Yeah. We get the wires kept coming in. You're coming in clear. Napoleon to St. Charles. Oh, I loved it. I have the write-ups there. Take me. It was a swell.
